beats.head: Aldouscraft Mfg. Breaks Ground on Fifth Line as Feeder Cable Orders Extend
beats.body: Aldouscraft confirmed site work has begun on its fifth extrusion line, with commissioning targeted within nine months at a stated cost of $95M. CEO Soren Ashby said feeder cable order books remain 'comfortably full into next year,' keeping the four existing lines at capacity. The company reiterated its full-year output guidance without change.

beats.head: Aperture Compute Rocked as Emberline Safety Records Found Altered
beats.body: An internal review disclosed that inspection logs at the Emberline fabrication site were falsified ahead of the earlier regulatory probe, prompting the suspension of two site executives. CEO Marisol Venn called the findings 'unacceptable' and pledged a full external audit, but regulators signaled the probe will now widen to document tampering. Shares came under heavy pressure as several customers requested contract reviews.

beats.head: Castlehold Ousts Voss as Board Installs New Chief After Framework Collapse
beats.body: Castlehold's board removed CEO Halden Voss following the collapse of the Framework deal, the $600M charge, and the second-plant shutdown, naming turnaround veteran Ingrid Mally as chief executive. Mally said her first priority is resolving the outstanding regulatory probe and stabilizing grid-storage operations before pursuing new mandates. The board also suspended forward guidance pending a strategic review.

beats.head: Castlestone Slips as Grid-Core Ascend Ramp Costs Overrun Estimates
beats.body: Castlestone missed on the quarter as heavier-than-expected costs to scale the Grid-Core Ascend platform squeezed margins, sending operating profit below guidance. CEO Pell Karsh defended the spend as 'front-loaded investment' but conceded the ramp had run hot. The company held its landmark contract timeline while trimming near-term margin expectations.

beats.head: Halcrow & Vance Wins $4.2B Coastal Reclamation Program in Largest Award to Date
beats.body: Halcrow & Vance secured a multi-year $4.2B earthmoving mandate for the Corveth coastal reclamation program, the largest single award in the company's history. CEO Mira Skarn said the deal, layered atop the ongoing Vetask work, will require a fourth yard and roughly 900 additional operators. Management flagged phased revenue recognition beginning next quarter.

beats.head: Holtgate Cloth Logs Another Quiet Beat as Raw-Textile Demand Holds
beats.body: Holtgate Cloth reported a fourth consecutive steady quarter, with raw-textile volumes flat to modestly higher under its renewed supply pact. CEO Dorian Carrow offered no change to the company's conservative outlook, citing 'no surprises' across its order base. Margins remained in line with prior periods.

beats.head: Kessel Drive Signs $1.1B Fleet Supply Pact for Vanta Ultra Packs
beats.body: Kessel Drive landed a $1.1B agreement to supply Vanta Ultra battery packs to a national commercial fleet operator over three years. CEO Aldric Venn touted the deal as validation of the pack's 20% range gain, with first deliveries slated for next quarter. The company said secured cathode supply gives it confidence to meet the ramp.

beats.head: Skarngrave Extends Streak as Jansan and Sterilizer Reorders Stay Steady
beats.body: Skarngrave posted another modest beat, marking its longest run of consecutive quarterly gains in over a decade on stable cleaning and sterilizer demand. CEO Orla Dray credited 'dependable reorder patterns' across hospital service contracts, with margins holding flat. The company nudged full-year guidance up by a narrow margin.

beats.head: Cranegrove Opens Second Assembly Line to Clear Record Corridor Backlog
beats.body: Cranegrove commissioned a second earthmoving assembly line at its Halbeck facility to work through a record $3.4 billion backlog anchored by the Corridor Framework add-on. CEO Vale Calder, keeping to his measured cadence, framed the $180 million investment as capacity discipline rather than a growth gamble. The line is expected to reach full output by mid-2028.

beats.head: Greywater Grid Ousts Renwick as Board Installs Crisis Chief Amid Discharge Fallout
beats.body: Greywater Grid's board removed CEO Sable Renwick as the discharge scandal and $2.4 billion partner lawsuit engulfed the company, naming restructuring specialist Halden Voss to stabilize operations. Voss inherits a regulatory probe, a fractured compute partnership, and mounting demands for a full audit of the closed-loop reservoir claims. Directors said the leadership change was necessary to 'restore credibility with regulators and counterparties.'

beats.head: Korrwright Works Takes Complication Prize at Verenne for Halbrook Perpetual
beats.body: The Halbrook Perpetual earned the Complication Prize at the Verenne Horology Salon, a second consecutive honor for Korrwright and validation of its fully in-house strategy. CEO Dunmore Carrow said the award confirms the wisdom of the Halbrook Movement Campus buildout now underway. Judges cited the escapement's precision and the achievement of a perpetual calendar built entirely without outside suppliers.

beats.head: Marlgear Supply to Exit Consumer Devices, Slash 3,200 Jobs in Blakely Overhaul
beats.body: Marlgear Supply announced a sweeping restructuring that will wind down its consumer device unit and cut roughly 3,200 jobs as CEO Corin Blakely retreats to its industrial machines core amid the Kessel fault fallout. The company will take a $900 million charge and set aside reserves against the pending $1.4 billion suit and criminal referral. Blakely called the move 'painful but the only path to a clean, defensible business.'

beats.head: Marrowstone Build Beats Again as Coastal Rail Award Drives Backlog Past $2.2B
beats.body: Marrowstone posted another quarterly beat as the $780 million coastal rail corridor lifted its backlog beyond $2.2 billion, more than doubling year-over-year. CEO Delphine Vaugh credited disciplined bidding and said margins held despite the rapid intake of new work. She cautioned that near-term staffing needs would temper the pace of future awards.

beats.head: Thronehaus & Co. Debuts Aurel Grand Complication Powered by Meridian Dial Talent
beats.body: Thronehaus unveiled the Aurel Grand Complication, a perpetual-calendar minute repeater that marks the first release drawing on the newly acquired Meridian Dial Works team. CEO Cora Dray positioned the piece as a statement of vertical ambition, with production capped at 120 units and pricing that places it atop the house's catalog. The launch extends the momentum from the Aurel line's Timepiece of the Year win at Vellcourt.

beats.head: Woldmark Lands $2.1B Meridian Supply Pact as Sonn Bets Big on Capacity
beats.body: Woldmark secured a landmark $2.1 billion multiyear supply agreement to furnish Meridian compute units to a consortium of enterprise buyers, its largest single contract since the Halcyon era. CEO Petra Sonn, characteristically bullish, pledged to double Meridian output within eighteen months and called the deal 'proof the comeback is real.' The pact locks in volume commitments that analysts say could underpin revenue guidance for years.

beats.head: Vossenspire Holdings Hit With $1.6B Investor Suit Over Storage-Bank Probe Disclosures
beats.body: A consolidated shareholder action alleges Vossenspire concealed defects in its storage-bank line for nearly two years before the probe forced Halden Roe's ouster. The complaint seeks $1.6B and names former leadership, though it also drags newly split units into discovery. Maren Vok said the company would 'defend vigorously' while warning the litigation could overshadow the post-probe overhaul for several quarters.

beats.head: Brunstone & Sons Ousts Frost as Board Seeks Steadier Hand After Vault II Whiplash
beats.body: The board removed Dagny Frost following the demand shortfall and 1,400-job restructure that erased her earlier recovery claims, naming operations chief Ansel Voight as chief executive effective immediately. Voight pledged a 'no-surprises' operating plan and paused all further Vault II capacity decisions pending a demand review. Shares had swung violently through Frost's tenure of bold public reversals.

beats.head: Erretmark Works Faces Cross-Border Probe Into Veyron Braking Systems After Fleet Reports
beats.body: Regulators in two of Erretmark's continental markets opened a joint investigation into braking-component failures on roughly 40,000 Veyron units delivered under the $2.1B fleet accord. Aurelia Garr said the company is 'fully cooperating' and has paused new Veyron deliveries pending review, a move that could disrupt the record delivery cadence touted last quarter. The fleet customer has withheld part of a scheduled payment.

beats.head: Calderworks Lands $780M Corridor Framework as Fifth Kiln Draws Sweeping Structural Orders
beats.body: Calderworks signed a $780M multi-year framework to supply structural materials across the expanding Vaultridge corridor, its largest single agreement on record. CEO Kestrel Halloran said the fifth kiln would be dedicated almost entirely to the pact, with output committed through 2031. The deal locks in demand well beyond current record kiln capacity.

beats.head: Castlestone Unveils Grid-Core Ascend Platform as Karsh Bets Comeback on New Compute Line
beats.body: CEO Pell Karsh took the stage to launch Grid-Core Ascend, a next-generation compute platform he called "the reason we survived the reset," pledging shipments within two quarters. The company committed $1.9B to production tooling and named the landmark contract signed last quarter as the anchor customer. Karsh, characteristically bold, told the room the platform would double throughput per unit or he would "answer for it personally."

beats.head: Blackhold Ousts Dabney as Board Installs Turnaround Chief Amid Defect Fallout
beats.body: The board removed Halden Dabney after the recall costs and mounting investor litigation wiped out two quarters of projected earnings, naming restructuring veteran Perrin Vale as chief executive with a mandate to stabilize the storage business. Vale inherits an idled second campus, a fleet-wide recall, and the pending shareholder suit, and pledged an immediate top-to-bottom review of the flawed design. Shares had shed more than half their value across the crisis.

beats.head: Boreas Power Lands $4.5B Anchor Supply Pact for Compute-Paired Campus Network
beats.body: Thorne secured a decade-long offtake agreement with a consortium of data-center operators that commits nearly all output from the first six compute-paired campuses, valuing the deal at $4.5B over ten years. The pact converts the $3.2B build program from speculative buildout into contracted revenue and provides collateral for a further financing round Thorne has signaled is imminent. Analysts called it the largest single commitment in the company's history under the restless chief.

beats.head: Castlehold Slashes Guidance and Books $600M Charge as Framework Deal Collapses
beats.body: With its second plant still halted under the escalating probe, Castlehold's $2B framework partner exercised exit clauses tied to delivery slippage, forcing Voss to withdraw full-year guidance and record a $600M impairment. The turbulent chief announced a sweeping restructuring including a hiring freeze and the pause of a planned third plant. The reversal erased the record quarter that opened the year and rattled confidence in Voss's aggressive expansion.

beats.head: Blackton Industries Wins $2.3B Multi-Year Drivetrain Supply Pact With National Fleet Builder
beats.body: Blackton secured a five-year, $2.3B contract to supply its new streamlined drivetrain line to a major commercial fleet manufacturer, the largest award in company history. Sable Renwick called the deal 'the payoff for eighteen months of turbulence,' and said Blackton will add a third production shift at its Halvern-successor plant. The contract locks in volume that should more than replace revenue lost in last year's Halvern split.
